q: Who developed an early ARPANET network email system in 1971 and used the @ sign to separate the user from the host?
explain: Ray Tomlinson developed network email in 1971 and chose @ to separate user and destination host.

q: In an email system, the storage space associated with an email account is called a:
explain: A mailbox stores the messages of an account. A packet is the unit in which data travels across the network.

q: Which of the following is a network designed for controlled access by outside parties, unlike an internal-only intranet?
explain: An extranet permits controlled outside access, while an intranet is internal to the organisation.

q: Hotmail, an early free webmail service, was founded by which pair?
explain: Hotmail was founded by Sabeer Bhatia and Jack Smith and launched on 4 July 1996. Jerry Yang and David Filo founded Yahoo.

q: In the email address student@example.com, what is 'student' called?
explain: The text before @ is the local part, commonly called the username. The text after @ is the domain.

q: Which of the following is a correctly structured email address?
explain: A valid address has exactly two parts separated by one @. The others have no @, two @ signs or a space.

q: Which characters are NOT permitted in a standard Gmail username?
explain: Standard Gmail usernames use a-z, 0-9 and periods only, normally 6-30 characters long.

q: The SMTP limit for the local part of an email address is:
explain: The local part is limited to 64 octets and the domain to 255 octets. The whole address normally fits in 254 octets, so the 320 figure is a myth.

q: Which statement about the complete email address length is correct?
options: It can always reach 320 characters by adding 64 + 1 + 255
It is limited to exactly 64 characters
It has no limit at all
explain: The SMTP path limit includes punctuation, so a complete mailbox address normally fits within 254 octets.

q: A browser-based way of accessing an email service, with no separate desktop program needed, is called:
explain: Webmail is a browser interface to an email service. An email client is an installed application such as Outlook.

q: Which of the following is an email client application rather than a webmail service?
explain: Thunderbird is an email client program. Rediffmail, Zoho Mail and Yandex Mail are webmail services.

q: Microsoft Outlook (the application) is both an email program and a:
explain: Outlook is a PIM: it handles calendars, contacts and tasks as well as email.

q: Which of the following is an email marketing platform, not a conventional personal mailbox?
explain: Mailchimp is a marketing platform with a limited free plan. Tuta, Proton Mail and iCloud Mail are mailbox services.

q: Gmail was launched by Google in which year, with Paul Buchheit as its key developer?
explain: Gmail launched on 1 April 2004. 1996 is Hotmail, 1997 is Yahoo Mail and 2011 is iCloud.

q: Yahoo Mail was launched in which year (the company itself began in 1994)?
explain: Yahoo began in 1994 with Jerry Yang and David Filo, but Yahoo Mail came in 1997.

q: Microsoft acquired Hotmail in which month and year?
explain: Hotmail launched in July 1996 and Microsoft bought it in December 1997; it later became Outlook.com.

q: iCloud, whose Mail service integrates with Apple devices, was launched on which date?
explain: iCloud launched on 12 October 2011. Yandex Mail dates from 26 June 2000.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of Gmail's five inbox categories?
explain: The five categories are Primary, Social, Promotions, Updates and Forums. Outbox is a sidebar item for messages waiting to be sent.

q: Receipts, confirmations and automated notices usually appear in which Gmail category?
explain: Updates collects receipts, confirmations and automated notices. Promotions holds offers and marketing mail.

q: Where would an unfinished message that you saved for later editing be found?
explain: Drafts hold unfinished messages. Outbox messages are complete but queued for sending.

q: A message is waiting to go out because the Internet connection is poor. Where does it normally stay in an email app?
explain: Messages queued for sending wait in the Outbox. Drafts are unfinished messages.

q: Which Gmail section includes archived mail but excludes Spam and Trash?
explain: All Mail covers archived mail too but leaves out Spam and Trash.

q: After how many days does Gmail normally delete messages in Trash permanently?
explain: Trashed messages are normally removed permanently after 30 days, unless you delete them earlier.

q: In an email, Bcc recipients are people whose addresses are:
options: Hidden from the To and Cc recipients
Hidden from the sender's sent copy
explain: Bcc (Blind Carbon Copy) hides those addresses from other recipients, though the sender can still see them in the sent copy.

q: What does Cc stand for in an email?
explain: Cc means Carbon Copy; those recipients get a visible copy.

q: Which command passes a received message on to a new person?
explain: Forward sends a received message to someone else. Reply answers the sender, and Reply all answers the sender plus the visible recipients.

q: Which statement about an email signature is correct?
options: It is the same as a cryptographic digital signature
It is a reusable closing block with name or contact details
It is required before any email can be sent
explain: A signature is just a reusable closing text block. A digital signature is a cryptographic feature that verifies authenticity.

q: Which protocol is used to send outgoing email and relay it between mail systems?
explain: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends and relays mail. POP3 and IMAP retrieve mail, and FTP transfers files.

q: Which protocol synchronises messages, folders and read status across several devices?
explain: IMAP works with a server-based mailbox so every device sees the same state. POP3 is download-oriented.

q: Which set correctly gives the basic (non-secure) port numbers of SMTP, POP3 and IMAP?
explain: SMTP uses 25, POP3 uses 110 and IMAP uses 143. 587, 995 and 993 are the secure/submission variants.

q: IMAP over implicit TLS uses which port?
explain: IMAP over implicit TLS uses 993. POP3 over implicit TLS uses 995 and SMTP submission over implicit TLS uses 465.

q: Which statement is correct about POP3 and IMAP?
options: POP3 sends mail and IMAP receives it
IMAP cannot be used for received mail
Both support access to received email
POP3 is technically limited to one device only
explain: Both retrieve received email. POP3 is download-oriented and IMAP is server-oriented; the one-device idea is only an exam shortcut.

q: MIME stands for:
explain: MIME means Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions; it extends email message formats for non-text content and non-ASCII text.

q: Which encoding is commonly used to represent binary attachments as ASCII-safe text for traditional mail transport?
explain: Base64 converts binary data into safe ASCII characters, because traditional SMTP was designed for 7-bit text.

q: In SMTP, which system acts as the SMTP client?
options: The one that accepts the connection
The one that initiates the transfer
explain: The system that starts the transfer is the SMTP client; the one accepting the connection is the SMTP server.

q: How many messages can a personal Gmail account generally send per day?
explain: Personal Gmail is generally limited to 500 messages a day. 2,000 is the paid Workspace figure and 1,500 is the mail-merge figure.

q: What is the total attachment size limit per message in personal Gmail?
explain: Personal Gmail allows 25 MB of attachments per message; larger files can be shared with a Google Drive link. 15 GB is the shared storage.

q: Which technology supports email encryption and digital signatures and is expanded as Pretty Good Privacy?
explain: PGP encrypts messages for confidentiality and signs them to verify authenticity.

q: Falsifying the sender information of an email to impersonate another sender is called:
explain: Spoofing fakes the sender. Phishing seeks sensitive information, sniffing captures traffic and skimming steals card data.

q: Phishing carried out through SMS or text messages is known as:
explain: Smishing is SMS phishing. Spoofing is faking a sender identity.
